Ethernet Switches Quick Installation Guide
Please read this instruction manual carefully before using the product and keep it properly.
1 Ethernet switch installation guide
Cautions
Install the devices
Connect the cables
Login the devices
LED indication
DIP switch indication
Notes
This user manual are for different models and include the installation methods, connection methods, LED indications and interface descriptions involved in various commercial Ethernet switch product models at present. Different product may have a little difference . Please refer to the actual situation to choose.
Cautions
In order to avoid equipment damage or personal injury caused by improper use, please take care of the following cautions :
Please make sure the switch is working under a correct and stable voltage.
Before using the switch, be sure to ground it via the ground screw.
Before cleaning the switch, the power plug of the switch should be pulled out first. Please do not wipe the switch with a wet cloth, and do not use liquid to clean the switch.
Please do not open the case when the switch is working. Even in the case of no power, do not open the switch case
Notes
This is a Class A equipment, in a domestic environment this product may cause radio interference. In such cases, the user may be required to take practicable measures against the interference.
Install the devices
According to different installation methods, Ethernet switches can be divided into two types: rack-mounted switches and desktop switches. The rack-mount switch supports two installation methods: desktop installation and rack-mount installation. The desktop switch supports two installation methods: wall-mount installation and desktop installation. Please check the different installation method as below. Different products have different installation method, please choose the suitable method
Rack-mount installation
It should be noted that the mounting ear of the Ethernet switch is not used for load bearing, it is only used for fixing on the rack. When installing the equipment on the rack, there must be a bracket (fixed on the cabinet) under the Ethernet switch to prop up it
The installation process is as below:
Please make sure the 19’’rack on good grounding.
Fixing the mounting ears on the both side of the switch.
Figure 1-1 Install the mounting ears
Place the switch on a bracket of the rack and move the switch along the guide rails of the rack to a proper position.
Use screws to install the Ethernet switch on the rack.
Figure 1-2: Install the Ethernet switch on the rack
Wall-mount installation
Take the 2-optical and 8-electrical switch as an example, place the switch at the location to be installed, and use a screwdriver to tighten the mounting ear screws on both sides.
Figure 1-3: Installation diagram
Desktop installation
Desktop installation directly place the device on the platform or desktop, and will not be described in detail here.
Connect the cables
Connect the configuration cable (only supported on managed switches)
The desktop switch and the rack-mount switch are connected to the configuration cable in the same way. Let’s take the rack-mount switch as an example. When configuring the switch through the terminal, the steps to connect the configuration cable are as follows:
Connect the USB plug of the configuration cable to the USB port of the computer.
Connect the RJ45 end of the configuration cable to the Console port of the Ethernet switch.
Figure 1-4: Connecting the Configuration Cable
Connecting the AC power cord
The installation process are as follows:
Connect one end of the power cord to the AC power plug of the device accurately and in place.
Connect the other end of the power cord to an external AC power outlet.
Figure 1-5: Connecting the AC Power Cord
Connecting the DC Power Cable
The installation process are as follows:
Make sure that the device is disconnected from the incoming power.
Connect one end of the protective grounding cable to the grounding screw of the equipment, and the other end is well grounded
Insert the DC end of the DC terminal of the power adapter into the DC socket of the device, and connect the other end to the mains supply, as shown in Figure 1-6 below.
Turn on the power supply and check the power indicator light on the front panel of the device. If the indicator light is on, it indicates that the power supply is normal.
Notes
The desktop Ethernet switch device supports DC 5-16V (non-PoE) and 44-57V (PoE) power supply.
Figure 1-6: DC socket power supply
Login the device（Accessing the switch for the first time）
There are two login methods for managed commercial Ethernet switch: WEB login management and Console login management.
Logging the switch through web-based
Open browser and enter 192.168.x.xxx in the address bar. (Google browser is recommended)；
Enter the use name: admin, password: admin, logging interface will be shown as Figure 1-7and Figure 1-8:
Figure 1-7: Success logging WEB interface(old version)
Figure 1-8: Success logging WEB interface(new version)
Logging the switch through console port.
Common serial port software includes SecureCRT and putty. Take SecureCRT for an example.
Open the SecureCRT, select ”New session”.
Select”Serial”, click “Next”.
Select relative COM port, baud rate 115200, flow control and delete the "√" on the RTS/CTS selectionbar, click “Next”, then click “Ok”.
Click” Enter”, input user name” admin”, password ”admin”. The logging interface will show as Figure 1-9
Figure 1-9
Recommendation/Suggestion
The configuration of managed switches is more complicated. It is recommended that users obtain configuration documents from the supplier before configuration. One is the Web configuration document and the other is the CLI configuration document.
Indicators and silkscreen of managed commercial Ethernet switch
The description of managed commercial Ethernet switch indicators
Table 1-1: Indicator status and silkscreen description
LED Indicators/Silkscreen	Status	Definition
P/PWR	Power Status indicator	Normal on	The device power on is normal
P/PWR	Power Status indicator	Off	The device is power off or failed
M/S	Unmanagement / System warning light / (Red light)	Normal on	PoE : the load power exceeds 90% of the rated power / Non-PoE : Chipset recognizing aberrant
M/S	Unmanagement / System warning light / (Red light)	Off	Devices no alarm
S/SYS	Management / System warning light / (Green light)	Normal on	The device is working normally
S/SYS	Management / System warning light / (Green light)	Blinking	The device is initializing
S/SYS	Management / System warning light / (Green light)	Off	The device is not powered on or it is faulty
USB	USB status indicator	Normal on	USB flash drive is detected by device
USB	USB status indicator	Blinking	the device is reading and writing the data from USB flash drive
USB	USB status indicator	Off	USB flash drive not insert or not detected by device
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Green light Link/act	Normal on	Ports link up
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Green light Link/act	Off	Ports link down
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Green light Link/act	Blinking	Data on TX/RX
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Yellow light Link/act	On	Ports on 1000M
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Yellow light Link/act	Off	Ports on 10/100M
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Yellow light PoE	On	PoE working
RJ-45 1000M Port LEDs	Yellow light PoE	Off	PoE not working
RJ-45 100M port indication	Green light Link/act	Normal on	Ports link up
RJ-45 100M port indication	Green light Link/act	Off	Ports link down
RJ-45 100M port indication	Green light Link/act	Blinking	Data on TX/RX
RJ-45 100M port indication	Yellow light Link/act	Normal on	Ports on 100M
RJ-45 100M port indication	Yellow light Link/act	Off	Ports on 10M
RJ-45 100M port indication	Yellow light PoE	Normal on	PoE working
RJ-45 100M port indication	Yellow light PoE	Off	PoE not working
SFP port indicator	Green light	Normal on	Ports link up
SFP port indicator	Green light	Off	Ports link down
SFP port indicator	Green light	Blinking	Data on TX/RX
reset button		Reset	Restore factory settings, long press ≥ 8 seconds
The definition of unmanaged commercial Ethernet switch DIP switch
Table 1-2: Unmanaged commercial Ethernet switch DIP switch comparison
Model Type / MMMmmmmModels TypeModels TypeModels Type / No	1	2	3	4
Non-PoE	V port (1-2) ①	Port isolation	VLAN	Port mirroring
PoE	V port (1-2) ①②	Port isolation	Remotely restart the PD device	250m long distance
Note:
① The packets of the V port are forwarded first when the network is congested,
②The V port is given priority for power supply when the power supply load is overloaded.
Table 1-3 Physical isolation media converter dip switch comparison
Status / No	1	2	3	4
ON	Forcing the copper port on 100M
OFF	Copper port 10/100/1000M adaptive
Note:
When the device are 8 channels isolated, there are two groups of DIP switches. The numbers of the two groups of DIP switches are 1,2,3,4.
